sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Adams County, Washington?
sections.html:
The Adams County Treasurer bills and collects property tax, and the Assessor sets the values the bill is built on. Call the Treasurer's office about balances and payments, and the Assessor at 509-659-3200 about exemptions and valuation.

The Treasurer does more than collect the annual bill. The office also acts as the Department of Revenue's agent for the real estate excise tax on property transfers, and it runs the foreclosure process on parcels that fall three years behind. Statements for each tax year should reach owners on or before March 15 under RCW 84.56.020, as long as the levy certifications arrive on time.

sections.h2: Adams County for a property owner
sections.html:
Adams County is a wheat and irrigated farming county in eastern Washington, with about 1,925 square miles of land and roughly 11 people per square mile. Ritzville is the county seat, in the northeast corner where Interstate 90 meets U.S. 395. Othello, in the southwest, is the largest city, and Hatton, Lind and Washtucna are the towns.

The 2025 estimate is 21,488 residents and 7,220 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the median value of an owner-occupied home was $273,300, and 69.3 percent of homes were owner-occupied. Much of the land is farm ground, which matters at sale time because agricultural parcels follow special excise tax rules, covered below.

The full tax is due by April 30. A bill over $50 can be split, with half due April 30 and the rest by October 31. Interest follows the schedule in RCW 84.56.020 and is applied to the full year's tax, not just the late half.

EventDate or rule
Statements due outMarch 15
First half or full yearApril 30
Second halfOctober 31
Interest, house or other residence of four units or fewer9 percent a year, no penalties
Interest, other property12 percent a year, plus 3 percent on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1
Tax lien attachesJanuary 1 of the year taxes are levied (RCW 84.60.020)
Foreclosure beginsAfter three full years of delinquency (RCW 84.64.050)

Mail with no readable postmark is still on time if the Treasurer receives it within three business days of the deadline. Ask the Treasurer's office for a current payoff amount, because interest is figured by the month.

sections.h2: Taxes and excise tax at a sale
sections.html:
The property tax lien runs from January 1. Unless the sale contract says otherwise, the seller owes the share of that year's tax for the days before the sale and the buyer owes the rest (RCW 84.60.020). Most contracts and escrow instructions settle this directly, so read yours.

Every transfer also needs a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit filed with the Treasurer before the deed is recorded at the Auditor. The county will not accept an incomplete affidavit, and forms must be on legal-size paper (8.5 by 14 inches).

  • Excise tax is due within 30 days of the sale date, and the Department of Revenue treats the notarized deed date as the date of sale.
  • The county adds a local 0.25 percent of the price plus a $5 processing fee to the state portion.
  • The state rate is graduated: 1.1 percent on the first slice, then 1.28, 2.75 and 3.0 percent. For sales starting January 1, 2027 the breakpoints are $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000.
  • Land classified as agricultural or timberland pays a flat 1.28 percent state rate if the buyer will keep using it that way and the Assessor signs the Notice of Continuance on the affidavit.

That last rule matters in a county built on farmland. Sellers of wheat ground or irrigated parcels should call the Assessor before the closing date, not after.

sections.h2: How do you challenge an assessed value?
sections.html:
You petition the county board of equalization on a Department of Revenue form. Under RCW 84.40.038 the petition is due by July 1 of the assessment year, within 30 days after the notice was mailed or sent electronically, or within a county-adopted limit of up to 60 days, whichever is latest.

The board may waive a late filing when the petition arrives within a reasonable time and the owner shows good cause. Listed causes include a death or serious illness in the immediate family, incorrect written advice from assessor or board staff, a natural disaster, and postal delay documented by the Postal Service. Call the Assessor at 509-659-3200 to learn which deadline your notice carries.

The county offers a senior citizen and disability exemption, and the Assessor is the office to call. Applicants must be at least 61 years old on December 31 of the application year, the home must be the principal residence on up to one acre, and household income must be $41,000 or less.

  • State law at RCW 84.36.381 also admits people retired because of disability and people receiving VA compensation at a service-connected rating of 40 percent or higher.
  • A person who sells or is displaced from a home can transfer exemption status to a replacement residence, though no one may claim it on more than one home in a year.
  • Tax statements carry a notice about the state deferral program in chapter 84.38 RCW.
  • For help with a mortgage or tax problem, the Washington Homeownership Resource Center answers at 877-894-4663.

sections.h2: What happens when taxes go unpaid for three years?
sections.html:
The Treasurer starts foreclosure. In July the Certificate of Delinquency is filed with Adams County Superior Court, foreclosure costs begin to accrue, and a title search is run on each parcel. Everyone with a recorded interest is served by certified mail, and the notice is also published in the county's official newspaper.

  • The court enters a judgment foreclosing the tax lien and authorizing a public auction.
  • Owners and others with a legal interest can redeem until the close of business the day before the sale.
  • Parcels that do not sell become Tax Title Property held in trust by the county, and a list is available by emailing the Treasurer.
  • A certificate of delinquency cannot be filed when the delinquent tax is $100 or less, excluding interest and penalties (RCW 84.64.050).

Personal property is handled differently: the treasurer is directed to seize and sell it once those taxes turn delinquent.

sections.h2: Preparing a cash sale of an Adams County property
sections.html: A sale with no lender moves on the schedule you and the buyer set. Before you list or accept an offer, call the Treasurer for the payoff, check with the Assessor about any agricultural classification or senior exemption on the parcel, and ask your escrow officer how the current year's tax will be split. Filing the excise tax affidavit with the Treasurer comes before the deed goes to the Auditor, and the tax itself is due within 30 days of the sale date.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Adams County, WA?
faqs.a: Full payment is due April 30, or half by April 30 and half by October 31 when the bill is over $50. Interest is figured by the month on late amounts.

faqs.q: What is the interest rate on late taxes in Adams County?
faqs.a: For a residence with four or fewer units the rate is 9 percent a year with no penalties. Other property pays 12 percent a year plus a 3 percent penalty on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1, under RCW 84.56.020.

faqs.q: Who pays real estate excise tax when I sell in Adams County?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays, and the buyer becomes responsible if the seller does not. The Treasurer collects it with the affidavit before the Auditor records the deed. The local share is 0.25 percent of the sale price, with a $5 processing fee.

faqs.q: How long does Adams County wait before foreclosing for unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Three full years. After that the Treasurer files a Certificate of Delinquency with the Superior Court in July, and the owner can redeem until the close of business the day before the auction.

faqs.q: Who can I call about the senior exemption in Adams County?
faqs.a: The Adams County Assessor's Office at 509-659-3200. Applicants must be at least 61 by December 31 of the application year, with a principal residence on up to one acre and income of $41,000 or less.
